submitter: vigilant designer + offer/benefit analyser lane — migration 780: content-listing gets its OWN carousel, forked from hero-card-carousel and made better (owner ruling 2026-09-04)
rationale:
OWNER RULING 2026-09-04, verbatim (relayed by the `boxingonline.com` lane): asked for the latest-articles section on boxingonline to become a carousel, he ruled *"it can have its own carousel forked from the best one and made better."*

**WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL — the request walks into a trap.** [MEASURED 2026-09-04] `boxingonline.com/index` carries three components: `content-listing` ("Latest from the site" — what he means, NO carousel field), `info-card-grid` ("A few places to start" — HAS one), and `call-to-action`. My migration `740` (approved, unapplied) defaults info-card-grid's carousel ON. **Applying 740 alone would put a carousel on his index page in the section he did not ask about**, while the one he did stayed a grid — readable as the request being actioned. 780 is what actually answers it.

⚠ I nearly missed that: my first query used `build_status='deployed' AND status='active'` and returned ZERO rows for the whole page, because the page is `needs_rebuild`. The pairing answers "what is SERVED"; "what is this page MADE OF" is `status='active'` alone. Filed as a landmine.

**WHICH IS "THE BEST ONE" — hero-card-carousel, and the judgement is on SEMANTICS, read rather than counted.** `hero-card-carousel` carries the actual ARIA carousel pattern: `role="region"`, `aria-roledescription="carousel"`, an `aria-label` from the section title, and per slide `role="group"` + `aria-roledescription="slide"` + a per-card label, plus a live region and `<ul>`/`<li>` track semantics. **`info-card-grid`'s carousel, when ON, emits `data-hcc-carousel data-hcc-autoplay="false"` and nothing else** — no role, no roledescription, no label; its cards get `data-hcc-slide` and no slide semantics. A screen reader is told nothing about it being a carousel. What info-card-grid DOES contribute is the opt-in gating that makes the off case byte-identical, which hero-card-carousel neither needs nor has. **This fork takes the semantics from one and the gating from the other.**

**"MADE BETTER" — one real improvement over BOTH: the track is focusable.** The shared snippet binds `root.addEventListener("keydown", …)` handling ArrowRight/ArrowLeft, and **neither existing template makes anything in the carousel focusable** — so today those keys are reachable only after tabbing onto an arrow BUTTON. `tabindex="0"` on the track gives the carousel itself a tab stop. ⚠ Stated precisely because I nearly claimed the opposite: **the keyboard handler EXISTS**; what was missing is anything focusable to deliver it. I read the JS before claiming.

**BYTE-IDENTITY WHEN OFF IS PROVEN, NOT CLAIMED.** Both templates rendered through Go `html/template` with identical data and diffed: carousel ABSENT + load_more true → IDENTICAL; ABSENT + load_more false → IDENTICAL; FALSE + load_more true → IDENTICAL; and TRUE vs FALSE → DIFFERENT as the control that the flag is not inert. On the ON render: `data-hcc-carousel` 1, `-track` 1, `-slide` 3, `-prev` 1, `-next` 1, `-live` 1, `aria-roledescription="carousel"` 1, `="slide"` 3, `tabindex="0"` 1, and "Load more" **0** against 1 when off. Every one reads 0 on the OFF render.

**That render check caught two defects review would not have.** (1) **A CSS COMMENT BECAME EXECUTABLE** — my style block explained the gating using the literal `{{if $.carousel}}` inside a `/* … */` comment, which Go's parser read as a real action, opening an `if` that never closed. The template failed with `unexpected EOF`; it would have gone into the live row invalid. (2) **A 1-CHARACTER DIFF THAT WAS THE INSTRUMENT** — the first diff came back one char short and looked like a real defect. It was `psql -At` appending a newline to the REFERENCE; the DB value is 1,526 chars and `right(html_template,1) = E'\n'` is FALSE.

**`show_load_more` — MY DECISION, NOT HIS, AND FLAGGED AS SUCH.** He did not address it. A horizontal carousel with a "Load more" button underneath is incoherent — the button implies a list growing downward, the carousel a track scrolling sideways. The carousel suppresses it. It is a one-key change if he disagrees, and the boxingonline lane is putting it to him rather than blocking. ⚠ It does not bite today anyway: boxingonline's instance already has `show_load_more: false`.

**DEFAULT-OFF, DELIBERATELY.** He said *"it can have its OWN"*, singular, answering a request about one section on one site. `content-listing` is **19 instances across 11 sites**. So: **no `fallback` on the field** (unlike 740), and `carousel: true` set on boxingonline's ONE instance explicitly. A further reason not to generalise, from the boxingonline lane: `bugs_open/444` — of 82 active index-family pages, 20 name NO listing and six share the identical `["hero","generic-text-block","call-to-action"]` signature across four sites. **On those pages there is no list to carousel.**

plan.summary: One appliable migration with four parts — a `carousel` boolean on content-listing's schema, the forked template, `content-listing` added to the hero-card-carousel snippet's applies_to, and carousel:true on boxingonline.com/index's single instance — plus a rollback that restores all four. No Go change, no image build, no dispatch.
plan.risks:
BLAST RADIUS IS DELIBERATELY ONE INSTANCE, and the guard for that is the important one. The field has NO fallback, so the other 18 instances across 10 sites are untouched. Proven by mutation: adding a fallback aborts with "would default ALL 19 instances ON, which the owner did not rule", and widening the instance UPDATE aborts with "19 instances carry carousel=true, expected 1".

THIS TOUCHES A PAYING CUSTOMER'S SITE, CONFIG ONLY. boxingonline is the first paid build and every dispatch there belongs to site_delivery_and_editor. This migration writes config; the page is already build_status='needs_rebuild' so it picks the change up on the rebuild THEY run. No dispatch from this lane.

ONE GUARD WAS VACUOUS AND ONLY THE MUTATION FOUND IT. The focusable-track assertion was `position('tabindex="0"' in tpl) = 0`, and stripping the attribute left it GREEN — because the template's own CSS comment explains the focusable track and contains that literal. A source-scanning assertion makes the COMMENTS load-bearing. Narrowed to `data-hcc-track tabindex="0"`, a markup-only string, and it now fires. Every guard here is a string search over a template that contains prose, so each needle was re-checked against the comments.

AND A MUTATION CAN ITSELF BE INVALID. My first ARIA mutation removed the first occurrence of the string in the .sql file, which was in the header prose rather than the template — the guard correctly stayed green and I nearly logged that as "the guard does not fire". Confirm the mutation landed where you meant before believing its result.

THE TEMPLATE IS PINNED BYTE-FOR-BYTE. The migration aborts unless the live template is exactly the text this fork was rendered and diffed against, so an intervening edit cannot be silently overwritten. Proven by mutation.

edits.rationale: All four parts with their drift guards and a separate verify block that re-reads the LIVE rows. Carried IN FULL — header, guards, the whole forked template and the entire verify — because this lane has twice drawn gating objections for showing only part of a verify block or asserting work done elsewhere.

Restores the template byte-for-byte, drops the field, filters content-listing out of applies_to and clears every instance flag — with a guard that the ORIGINAL two applies_to entries survive, since a bad jsonb_agg filter could empty the array. States what it does NOT undo: a page already rendered as a carousel keeps its stored HTML until it re-renders.
